name: chrome-devtools-mcp
one_liner: A plug-in that lets AI coding assistants drive a real Chrome browser — click buttons, read network traffic, take screenshots, and diagnose slow pages — instead of guessing what a webpage is doing.
buyer: A software agency or QA team building AI-assisted testing or debugging tools for web apps.
business_use_cases: A QA automation startup builds an AI test-writing product on top of it so an agent can click through a site and report what broke.
A web performance consultancy uses it to have an AI agent automatically audit client sites and draft a performance report.
A dev-tools vendor bundles it into an 'AI pair programmer that can actually see the browser' feature for their coding assistant product.

money_ideas.idea: Build a paid SaaS that runs automated AI-driven site audits (performance, broken links, console errors) using it under the hood
Offer it as part of a billed-by-usage AI QA testing API for other dev tools to call

steal_this: Wrap it into a 'point an AI at any URL and get a bug/performance report' web tool — free scan, paid PDF report with fixes, since the hard browser-control part is already solved for you.
